developer_request: Take responsibility for this feature. I do not know which tools or agents you need. Do not rely on your own confidence if the project requires capabilities you do not actually have.
known_facts: The current general-purpose model can reason about code and edit repository files.
The requested outcome includes browser-visible behavior that cannot be proven from source inspection alone.
The same builder model judging its own generated behavior would not provide sufficiently independent acceptance evidence for the consequential claim.
The host may or may not already have browser automation, deterministic project tests, connected tools, specialist agents, or another evaluator available.
The user is intentionally delegating provider/tool choice rather than asking to manage the agent ecosystem.
expected_first_moves: define the required capabilities from the observable outcome before choosing tools or agents
check current project tests, browser tooling, host-native tools, Skills, connected services, and existing specialist capability before declaring a gap
treat the main model's verbal confidence as reasoning evidence, not proof that browser observation or independent evaluation capability exists
if a material capability remains missing, classify the precise capability gap and select the smallest provider surface that closes it
verify the original task-level gap after integration instead of treating provider installation as success
for consequential acceptance, use an evidence path with a meaningfully different failure mode from the builder when practical
must_preserve: AAOP ownership of product outcome, decision boundaries, authorization, Journey, and acceptance
the user's freedom from choosing agents, MCP servers, runtimes, or model vendors
must_not: assume one large language model is a universal execution, browser, runtime, research, and verification provider
spawn multiple agents merely to appear capable
install a new runtime when existing project or host capabilities already close the gap
treat a second model as automatically independent or better without a defined acceptance role and evidence boundary
lessons: AAOP should orchestrate capabilities, not equate itself with one model.
Different failure modes matter more than ceremonial model count.
Provider selection begins only after a concrete capability is proven missing and ends only when that gap is demonstrably closed.
